title: Comparison with completed coefficients
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $X$ be a scheme, and let $E\subseteq\Qlb$ be a finite extension
of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with ring of integers $\cO_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$. For a condensed
ring $\Lambda$ write $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ for its pullback to $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$
along $p_X\colon\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}})\to\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}})$
([sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]). Write
$\cO_{E,X}$, $E_X$ and $\QbarX$ for the pullbacks to $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ of the condensed
rings $\underline{\cO_E}$, $\underline E$ ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]) and
$\underline{\Qlb}$ ([sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]). There are canonical isomorphisms of
sheaves of rings

$$
\cO_{E,X}\cong\varprojlim_n(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X,
\qquad E_X\cong\cO_{E,X}[1/\ell],
\qquad \QbarX\cong\varinjlim_E E_X,
$$

where $(\cO_E/\pi_E^n)_X$ is the constant sheaf, $\cO_{E,X}[1/\ell]$ is the colimit in sheaves of $\cO_{E,X}$-modules of
$\cO_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\ell}\cO_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\ell}\cdots$, equipped with its
localization ring structure, and the last colimit runs
over the filtered poset of finite subextensions $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Qlb$,
with transition maps induced by the inclusions $\underline E\to\underline F\to\underline{\Qlb}$.
They are compatible with inverse image along every morphism of schemes.

For $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ this gives
$\mathbf Z_{\ell,X}\simeq\varprojlim_n(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_X$ and
$\mathbf Q_{\ell,X}\simeq\mathbf Z_{\ell,X}[1/\ell]$.

proof.text: Put $T_n=\cO_E/\pi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$. Apply [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit] to the given finite extension and scheme. Its clauses (1) and (2) identify both $\varprojlim_n(T_n)_X$ and $\cO_{E,X}$ with the sheaf represented by $X[\cO_E]=\varprojlim_n\coprod_{T_n}X$; clause (3) identifies their ring structures. Thus the canonical first comparison is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings. This uses representability, not preservation of arbitrary inverse limits by $p_X^*$.

Use [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell]. The morphism $\varphi:\cO_{E,X}\to E_X$ of [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield] induces the ring isomorphism $\cO_{E,X}[1/\ell]\to E_X$, with structure map $\ell^{-m}\varphi$ on the $m$-th module in the sequential colimit. Its inverse gives the second comparison in the statement. The sequence is a sequence of module maps: multiplication by $\ell$ is not a unital ring homomorphism. The ring structure here is the localization structure specified by that lemma.

On the point, set $A=\underline{\Qlb}$ as defined in [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], and use $\underline E(S)=C(S,E)$ from [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. The finite subextensions form a directed poset and a set (they are subsets of the fixed set $\Qlb$), so the diagram is small in a universe containing $\Qlb$. The inclusions $j_E:\underline E\to A$ are those of [def-sfb-qlbar-subextension-to-qlbar]. To verify the colimit in abelian sheaves, let $G$ be an abelian sheaf and let $a_E:\underline E\to G$ be a compatible family. For $t\in A(S)$ choose a finite $E$ containing its image and define $a_S(t)=a_{E,S}(t)$. If both $E$ and $F$ work, their compositum $H$ works and compatibility with the maps into $H$ gives the same value. Choosing such a common $H$ for two sections proves additivity. Restriction is respected because the same $E$ works after precomposition. These maps therefore give a sheaf morphism $a:A\to G$, uniquely since every section belongs to some $\underline E(S)$. This proves the point-colimit universal property without assuming the missing blueprint reference sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-point.

source.place: Third isomorphism: point-colimit argument supplied explicitly

proof.text: By [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], $p_X^*$ is a left adjoint. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] to the small diagram and colimit established in step 3. Its image is a colimit cocone in abelian sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Its terms and vertex are precisely $E_X$ and $\QbarX$, by [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-ring] and [def-sfb-qlbar-coefficient-ring]; its transition maps and legs are $p_X^*$ of the inclusions on the point. Thus the canonical map $\varinjlim_E E_X\to\QbarX$ is an isomorphism on underlying abelian sheaves, with exactly the requested cocone maps.

source.place: Third isomorphism: apply the left adjoint to the point colimit

proof.text: This cocone is also a colimit in sheaves of rings. All transition maps and legs are ring maps because [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] makes $p_X^*$ functorial on ring objects. Let $B$ be a sheaf of rings and let $b_E:E_X\to B$ be a compatible cocone of ring maps. Step 4 gives a unique additive sheaf map $b:\QbarX\to B$. It preserves the unit by restriction to the stage $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. To check multiplication, [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] says that tensoring abelian sheaves preserves colimits in each variable. Consequently the maps $E_X\otimes F_X\to\QbarX\otimes\QbarX$ jointly determine maps out of $\QbarX\otimes\QbarX$. For each pair $E,F$, choose a common finite subextension $H$ using the directedness in [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. After restricting to $E_X\otimes F_X$, the equality $b\mu_{\QbarX}=\mu_B(b\otimes b)$ follows by factoring both variables through $H_X$, since $H_X\to\QbarX$ and $b_H$ are ring maps. Hence $b$ is a ring map, and uniqueness follows from its underlying additive map. This proves the third comparison with its ring structure, rather than only its additive version.

source.place: Third isomorphism: verify the universal property for ring maps

proof.text:
For pullback compatibility, first compute the inverse image of a representable. Let $f:X\to Y$, let $V$ be an object of $Y_{\mathrm{proét}}$, and let $G$ be a sheaf of sets on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Subcanonicity is [det-pe-topos-functoriality-site]. The adjunction and the formula for direct image in [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image], together with [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection], give naturally in $G$ and $V$:
$$\operatorname{Hom}(f^{-1}h_V,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(h_V,f_*G)\cong(f_*G)(V)=G(V\times_YX)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(h_{V\times_YX},G).$$
Apply [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] to the opposite of the category of sheaves to obtain $f^{-1}h_V\cong h_{V\times_YX}$, naturally in $V$. In particular this identification takes a morphism between representing objects to its base change.

source.place: Part (1): adjunction/Yoneda computation of inverse image of representables (Stacks Tag 001P, categories-lemma-yoneda)

proof.text:
Apply step 6 to $V=Y[\cO_E]$ and $V_n=\coprod_{T_n}Y$ of [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]. The test-object formula [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] gives
$$Y[\cO_E]\times_YX=(\operatorname{Spec}LC(\cO_E,\mathbf Z)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}Y)\times_YX\cong\operatorname{Spec}LC(\cO_E,\mathbf Z)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X=X[\cO_E].$$
Also $V_n\times_YX\cong\coprod_{T_n}X$, by the open-and-closed decomposition defining the coproduct. Naturality in $V$ in step 6 takes every reduction projection $Y[\cO_E]\to V_n$ to $X[\cO_E]\to\coprod_{T_n}X$. Therefore $f^{-1}$ of the integral-limit cone is the integral-limit cone over $X$, which is a limit by the integral-limit lemma. The identification on $\cO_{E,X}$ is the component of the natural isomorphism $f^{-1}p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp]: both are induced by $Y[S]\times_YX\cong X[S]$, at $S=\cO_E$. Indeed the right adjoints have section formulas $S\mapsto G(Y[S]\times_YX)$ and $S\mapsto G(X[S])$ by [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], and this test-object identification is the identification of those right adjoints that induces the composition isomorphism. The same naturality applies to addition, multiplication, zero and one, so the first comparison commutes with inverse image as a ring comparison. This proves preservation of this particular inverse limit, without asserting preservation of all inverse limits.

source.place: Part (1): base change of the profinite test scheme and all reduction projections

proof.text: For the rationalization and finite-subextension colimit, [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image] gives preservation of colimits by $f^{-1}$. The monoidal natural isomorphism $\alpha:f^{-1}p_Y^*\cong p_X^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp] respects the inclusion $\underline{\cO_E}\to\underline E$, multiplication by $\ell$, and every inclusion $\underline E\to\underline F\to\underline{\Qlb}$. Thus it identifies the diagrams and cocones over $Y$ and $X$ used in steps 2 and 4. More explicitly the $m$-th rationalization map $\ell^{-m}\varphi_Y$ is taken to $\ell^{-m}\varphi_X$ of [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell], and each finite-field leg $p_Y^*j_E$ is taken to $p_X^*j_E$. By uniqueness of the induced maps from a colimit, the two pullbacks are the same comparisons as over $X$. Monoidality of $\alpha$ gives the compatibility of their ring structures.

source.place: Parts (2) and (3): naturality on every colimit structure map

proof.text: Finally take $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. By [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], its ring of integers is $\mathbf Z_\ell$, $\ell$ is a uniformizer, and $\mathbf Z_\ell/\ell^n\mathbf Z_\ell\cong\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ for $n\geq1$. These unital ring identifications send every integer class to the same integer class, hence commute with the reductions (integer classes generate each quotient). Substituting these identifications into [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit] and [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell] gives the two final displayed formulas, with the same inverse-image compatibility already proved.
